main_issues: Assurance language is too specific and implies assurance may have been obtained for Scope 1 and Scope 2, which is not evidenced here and conflicts with the stated lack of detailed operational GHG data.
Transparency gap: the evidence package explicitly flags use of synthetic/generated data at report level, but the draft does not disclose this boundary.

Some “section will include” descriptions (governance/strategy/risk/metrics) risk overpromising content breadth; General Requirements should describe what the Bank discloses, not what internal records exist.
required_fixes: Revise the assurance paragraph to remove any implication that external assurance was obtained unless the Bank can cite the assurance provider, scope, standard, and location. If unknown/absent, state plainly that the report is not externally assured and do not mention Scope 1/2 assurance.

Add a clear report-level transparency statement that some information/metrics may be based on synthetic/generated data or modelled estimates (as applicable), and explain at a high level where this occurs (eg, scenario analysis, financed emissions estimation), without using report-machinery terms.

Align operational GHG boundary wording with the evidence boundary: avoid suggesting Scope 1/2 assurance or detailed operational emissions coverage when operational GHG records are not available; keep the limitation explicit and consistent.

Tighten “what the sections contain” statements to avoid overclaiming (eg, replace broad claims about committee structures/skills/remuneration linkages with narrower wording that matches what is actually disclosed in the report).
unsupported_claims: “The report is not externally assured as a whole. Any external assurance, where obtained, is limited to selected greenhouse gas information relating to Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.” (Assurance existence is not evidenced in the General Requirements evidence package; only a boundary flag indicates assurance evidence exists, without specifying that assurance was actually obtained for this reporting period/report.)

“The Governance section describes key elements of Board and management oversight … including information on committee structures, meeting frequency, skills and remuneration linkages …” (The evidence package indicates some governance metrics exist, but this sentence risks overpromising breadth—eg, committee structures and meeting frequency may be present, but “skills” and “remuneration linkages” should be stated as what is actually disclosed, not what records exist.)

“The Strategy section outlines … including the use of climate scenario analysis where available.” (Scenario analysis exists in other section payload keys, but General Requirements evidence does not itself evidence that scenario analysis is actually used/disclosed in the Strategy section as drafted; acceptable if the Strategy section indeed contains it, but as a standalone evaluation this is a mild support gap.)
material_unsupported_claims: External assurance wording implies assurance may have been obtained for Scope 1 and Scope 2. Given operational GHG records are flagged as not available, and the evidence package does not provide an assurance statement or scope details for the reporting period, this must be reframed to avoid implying assurance was obtained (eg, state the Bank does not obtain external assurance for this report; if assurance is obtained in future/elsewhere, specify location and scope).
minor_wording_to_tighten: “This report sets out … climate‑ and sustainability‑related financial disclosures.” (Fine, but could clarify that the report focuses primarily on climate, with broader sustainability only to the extent addressed, to avoid implying full S1 breadth.)
“These horizons are intended to be broadly consistent with the Bank’s internal strategic and risk planning cycles.” (Defensible; could be tightened to “are aligned to” only if evidenced.)

“The Bank seeks to describe the nature of the metrics and key limitations at a high level in the relevant sections of the report.” (Could be tightened to avoid implying this is consistently done unless confirmed in the core sections.)
available_evidence_omitted: Report-level boundary that the report uses synthetic or generated data (report_level_boundaries.uses_synthetic_or_generated_data=true) is not disclosed anywhere in General Requirements.

Known evidence boundary that operational GHG records are not available (operational_ghg_records_available=false) is not explicitly reflected; draft instead implies selected Scope 1 and Scope 2 information exists and may be assured.

Known evidence boundary that methodology records are not available (methodology_records_available=false) is only partially reflected; draft says detailed methodologies are not disclosed, but does not clearly state they are not currently available/maintained at the level needed for disclosure.

main_issues: One factual inconsistency in trend disclosure: 2023 all-executive climate-linked remuneration is misstated (draft: 15.3% in 2023 is correct in evidence, but the draft’s three-year trend presentation omits it from the narrative structure by not clearly presenting all three years consistently; the bigger issue is that the trend is presented but not fully/cleanly evidenced in the same way as CEO trend).

Two over-strong governance assertions that go beyond the compact evidence: (i) broad claim of integration into overall corporate governance framework; (ii) committee described as having an ongoing pre-submission review role for targets/methodologies/plans.
required_fixes: Correct and complete the three-year trend for all-executive climate-linked remuneration by explicitly including 2022 (8.7%), 2023 (15.3%) and 2024 (15.1%) in the same way the CEO trend is presented.

Reframe the opening 'integrates climate-related governance into its overall corporate governance framework' to a narrower, evidence-anchored description of the specific governance mechanisms used (Board agenda coverage, committee oversight, semi-annual reporting, risk register, ERM integration flags, transaction checks, remuneration linkages).

Rephrase the ESG & Sustainability Committee role statement from an ongoing process claim ('prepares... and is involved in reviewing... before submission') to a fact-based description anchored to 2024 activities/decisions (e.g., it considered scenario methodology and transition plan matters and reported to the Board).

Where ERM integration is described, consistently qualify it as an ERM integration flag at bank level and per-risk flags (6 of 8 risks), avoiding any implication of full integration across all climate risks.
unsupported_claims: Overview: 'integration of climate-related risks into the enterprise risk management framework' could be read as full integration; the evidence supports an ERM integration flag at bank level and per-risk flags for 6/8 risks, but not comprehensive integration across all climate risks.

Overview: 'documented 2024 Board and committee decisions' is supported, but the surrounding phrasing implies a broader governance system than evidenced (see material_unsupported_claims on over-strong framing).
material_unsupported_claims: Overview: 'Eurolux Universal Bank AG integrates climate-related governance into its overall corporate governance framework.' This is broader than the evidence provided (which supports specific mechanisms—agenda coverage, committee existence/activity, semi-annual reporting, ERM integration flags, risk register use, transaction checks, remuneration linkages—but not an overarching integration into the full corporate governance framework). Reframe to describe the evidenced mechanisms without asserting enterprise-wide integration.

Board committees subsection: 'is involved in reviewing climate-related targets, methodologies and plans before they are submitted to the Board.' Evidence supports committee/board decisions on scenario methodology and transition plan endorsement, but does not evidence a standing pre-submission review role across targets/methodologies/plans as a defined process. Reframe to 'considered' or 'reviewed in 2024' rather than asserting an ongoing role.
minor_wording_to_tighten: Board role subsection: 'This trend indicates...' (agenda coverage and expertise trends). Consider neutral phrasing ('Climate-related topics appeared on the agenda in...') to avoid implying causality or qualitative conclusions beyond the metric.

Management subsection: 'Climate checks for major transactions are recorded as part of management processes.' Tighten to avoid implying a formalised process framework; evidence supports that checks occur, but not a formal mandatory policy.

Management subsection: 'The register also records mitigation actions at the risk level.' Supported by mitigation-action fields, but consider clarifying these are recorded actions rather than confirmed implemented controls.
available_evidence_omitted: Explicit statement that the Bank is under the CSRD regulatory regime (contextual; not required but available).

Explicit statement of the assurance standard (ISAE 3000) is included, but the draft does not explicitly restate the assurance level as 'limited' in the assurance sentence (it is implied elsewhere; could be made explicit).

main_issues: Current-period financial effects are handled as a boundary, but the draft could better meet IFRS S1 Strategy expectations by identifying which primary financial statement line items are most likely to be affected (qualitatively) even if not quantified.
A few statements read stronger than the underlying support (notably ‘on track’ and Pillar 2 threshold phrasing) and should be explicitly bounded to avoid an assurance-like impression.
Capex/opex narrative attributes spending to initiative types without clear support; should be framed as indicative examples.
required_fixes: Strengthen the ‘financial effects’ subsection by adding qualitative identification of the most likely affected line items/totals/subtotals (eg, impairment/ECL, RWA, net interest income, fee income, operating expenses), while keeping the existing boundary that impacts are not yet quantified.

Reframe target progress language to avoid over-assertion: keep the summary (type/scope/year/framework/progress) and explicitly state that the Strategy section does not disclose baselines, interim milestones, validation/assurance, gross/net treatment or carbon credit use; present ‘on track’ as an internal status assessment rather than a guaranteed outcome.

Tighten resilience wording: keep scenario-specific conclusions, but avoid implying undisclosed quantified Pillar 2 thresholds; use wording consistent with internal buffer expectations unless thresholds are disclosed elsewhere.
Adjust capex/opex description so initiative references are clearly illustrative (eg, ‘includes investments in…’) rather than implying a verified allocation mapping.
unsupported_claims: “The Bank allocated climate-related capital expenditure of 476.95 million euro and climate-related operating expenditure of 219.32 million euro. These amounts relate to initiatives such as sustainable finance platform development, data and systems for climate risk assessment, and energy efficiency measures in own operations.” (Amounts are supported; the specific initiative-level attribution is not evidenced in the compact evidence and should be framed as examples rather than asserted allocation mapping.)

“In orderly scenarios, transition risk losses remain within Pillar 2 capital buffer thresholds …” (Supported by scenario resilience summary, but ‘thresholds’ implies a defined quantified limit; should be phrased as ‘within the Bank’s Pillar 2 buffer expectations/management thresholds’ unless the thresholds are disclosed elsewhere.)
material_unsupported_claims: “All three targets are currently assessed as on track …” (Target status is supported, but presenting ‘on track’ without stating that only a summary is disclosed can be read as a strong assurance-like claim; it should be explicitly bounded in the Strategy narrative that the assessment is based on internal tracking and that baseline/milestones/validation details are not disclosed in this section.)
minor_wording_to_tighten: “Dedicated climate-related capital and operating expenditure support implementation.” (Fine, but could be tightened to avoid implying ring-fenced budgets if not separately tracked as such.)

“The lending book is the primary transmission channel … complemented by actions in own operations and procurement.” (Supported directionally; could clarify that upstream procurement is assessed qualitatively.)
“Carbon price trajectories from international net-zero pathways …” (Tighten to the stated methodology: IEA NZE 2050 trajectory mapping, if that is the Bank’s approach.)
available_evidence_omitted: Scenario methodology detail that orderly scenarios map carbon prices using an IEA NZE 2050 trajectory (draft refers generically to 'international net-zero pathways' rather than specifying the IEA NZE mapping used in the methodology summary).

Risk register count context (risk_register_count=16) is not referenced; draft states eight material risks (which is correct) but does not clarify that the register contains additional non-material items.

main_issues: Industry-based banking guidance gap: the draft does not describe the Bank’s approach to incorporating ESG/climate factors into credit analysis (and only states a boundary for ECL).

Occasional slippage from ‘recorded mitigation actions’ to implied ‘implemented controls/procedures’, which increases over-claim risk given the explicit boundary that detailed procedures are not disclosed.

IFRS S1 risk management requirement is flagged as possibly missing by the pre-check; while the draft describes register mechanics, it still reads more like an inventory than a process description (inputs/parameters, decision-use, and how identification/assessment is performed in practice are thin).
required_fixes: Add a concise, bank-voice description of how climate/ESG factors are incorporated into credit analysis for lending decisions (e.g., where in the credit process climate factors are considered, what types of borrower/collateral attributes are assessed, and how this influences creditworthiness views), without claiming ECL integration if not disclosed.

Systematically reframe mitigation statements to avoid implying formalised controls or uniform implementation. Use consistent language such as ‘the register records the following mitigation actions for specific risks’ and avoid ‘applied’ unless the Bank is prepared to assert implementation.

Strengthen the ‘process’ narrative (identify–assess–prioritise–monitor) using only evidenced elements: classification into physical/transition categories, ratings, time horizons, monitoring cadence, scenario-linking for selected risks, and ERM integration flagging; avoid implying additional governance/escalation/limit-setting.

Optionally tighten scenario analysis description with one definitive sentence stating the scenario set is based on NGFS v4 and comprises 18 scenarios, and that four scenario identifiers are referenced by five risks in the register.
unsupported_claims: “Mitigation actions … include: climate scenario stress testing integrated into the internal capital adequacy assessment process, collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlays, engagement and transition-plan covenants with borrowers, green retrofit financing incentives, portfolio decarbonisation glide-path monitoring and sector exposure limits with enhanced due diligence.” (Supported as register-listed actions, but the draft sometimes implies operational implementation beyond what is evidenced.)

“The Bank’s climate-related risk management information is connected to its broader sustainability and climate strategy and to the metrics and targets disclosed elsewhere in this report.” (Connection is asserted but not demonstrated within this section; acceptable if cross-references exist elsewhere, but not evidenced here.)
material_unsupported_claims: “Mitigation actions … include … collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlays …” and similar action statements are presented in places as if they are implemented controls/processes. The evidence supports that these are recorded mitigation actions in the register, but not that they are implemented as formalised, bank-wide day-to-day procedures. This needs consistent framing as ‘recorded actions’ rather than implying operational effectiveness or uniform application.
minor_wording_to_tighten: “The register provides a structured view of climate-related risks that could affect the Bank’s lending portfolios and related activities.” (Tighten to ‘lending and credit portfolios’ to match the register scope described elsewhere.)

“Scenario analysis is used as a forward-looking input…” (Good boundary; consider adding that it is applied to selected risks only, each linked in the register, to avoid any inference of portfolio-wide application.)
available_evidence_omitted: Explicit statement that the scenario analysis framework used is NGFS v4 (the draft mentions NGFS v4, but does not clearly state it as the framework used for the Bank’s scenario set in one definitive sentence).

Explicit enumeration that the Bank’s scenario set comprises 18 scenarios (the draft references a broader set of 18, but could state the count more directly as part of the scenario analysis description).

main_issues: Financed emissions intensity target baseline/milestones (20.0 / 18.2 / 15.8 tCO₂e per EURm) are not reconcilable with the disclosed 2024 portfolio carbon intensity (1,154.81 tCO₂e per EURm) as presented; the draft implies they are the same metric used for monitoring.

IFRS alignment is generally asserted but key IFRS S1 metric-definition expectations (definition/source, calculation method/inputs, and consistency over time) are only addressed as a broad limitation; this is acceptable given methodology unavailability, but the draft should avoid implying comparability/IFRS-preparedness beyond what is supported.
Governance oversight is referenced, but remuneration linkage is not addressed (the draft states it is not detailed). This is a completeness limitation rather than an evidence contradiction.
required_fixes: Fix the financed emissions intensity target monitoring narrative: either (a) explain clearly that the target-record intensity metric uses a different definition/perimeter/denominator than the disclosed 2024 portfolio carbon intensity and therefore is not directly comparable, or (b) correct the target intensity baseline/milestones to match the same intensity definition used for the 2024 metric, or (c) remove the statement that the 2024 intensity metric is used to monitor performance against that specific target and instead state that the Bank monitors financed emissions intensity using the disclosed portfolio metric while the target-record intensity metric is defined separately (definition not disclosed).

Add a short, explicit metric-definition note for each key metric (financed emissions, intensity, high-carbon exposure, fossil-fuel exposure, green loans, climate capex/opex) stating that detailed calculation methods/criteria are not described in this report (already stated generally) and, where relevant, clarify the denominator and point-in-time basis (e.g., exposures as at 31 Dec 2024).

If retaining statements about IFRS S1/S2 reference, add a brief clarification that the Bank’s disclosures are prepared with reference to IFRS S1/S2 requirements but that certain required details (e.g., calculation methodologies and disaggregation) are not yet provided in this report.
unsupported_claims: “These metrics are prepared with reference to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2” (general alignment claim without accompanying basis-of-preparation detail in this section).

“The target record identifies the Net-Zero Banking Alliance as the target framework and indicates that the target uses a sectoral decarbonisation approach.” (framework/method approach is supported by target-record fields, but the draft then links monitoring to a 2024 intensity metric that is not directionally consistent with the baseline intensity in the target record, creating an implied progress narrative that is not substantiated).

“The financed emissions intensity target is supported by the 2024 portfolio carbon intensity metric of 1,154.81 tCO₂e per EUR million of lending, which is used to monitor performance against the target.” (creates an apparent inconsistency with the target baseline intensity of 20.0 tCO₂e/EURm and milestones of 18.2 and 15.8).
material_unsupported_claims: Implied coherence between the financed emissions intensity target baseline/milestones (20.0; 18.2; 15.8 tCO₂e/EURm) and the disclosed 2024 portfolio carbon intensity (1,154.81 tCO₂e/EURm). As drafted, stating the 2024 metric is used to monitor progress against that target is not credible without an explanation of differing definitions/perimeters/denominators or a correction of the target-record intensity units/values.
minor_wording_to_tighten: “focus on … medium- and long-term greenhouse gas reduction targets” (targets include 2030 and 2050; consider explicitly stating time horizons rather than qualitative labels).

“These loans include financing that supports low-carbon and climate-resilient activities” (define the green loan taxonomy/criteria or explicitly state that the classification methodology is not described in this report).
“provide a decision-useful overview” (acceptable, but could be softened given the stated methodology and disaggregation gaps).
available_evidence_omitted: Target-record status fields (e.g., 'on_track') are not disclosed for any of the three targets, despite being available in the target records.
Target-record 'latest_paris_alignment' fields are not disclosed (the draft instead states it does not confirm Paris alignment).

warnings.details: Prefer validation/verification wording in Metrics and targets.
